argument:
The bull correctly retains RM445m post-capex/lease cash and RM141m realised savings as evidence of an operating repair resource. Savings cannot be added again to that cash bridge, and its explicit acceptance of the RM376m dividend gap answers an overclaimed payout thesis. It does not show that efficiencies are presently closing the gap.

Statutory CFO fell from RM1.516bn to RM1.222bn, borrowing rose to RM14.461bn, and normalised PAT growth was only 0.9%. At 19.31x earnings and 5.42% reported yield, modest growth and thin cash compensation leave material exposure to slower integration. The H2FY2027 milestone is prospective; payout restraint is not an observed decision. Positive post-lease cash makes recovery possible, but current cash deterioration and uncovered distributions remain stronger purchase objections than the oversold chart can offset.
key_points: Post-lease cash and savings provide a genuine repair resource.
Statutory cash fell and distributions remain uncovered.
Modest growth limits valuation compensation for integration risk.
rebuttal_to_previous: The bull answers whether repair is financially conceivable and avoids double-counting savings. It has not demonstrated cash improvement or payout adjustment, so the observed funding gap remains unresolved at the quoted income valuation.
